person.name: Alan_Turing
person.summary: English mathematician and computer science pioneer whose 1936 paper formalised computation via the Turing machine; key World War II cryptanalyst at Bletchley Park; postwar designer of the ACE computer; contributor to the philosophy of AI (Turing test) and mathematical biology (morphogenesis).

events.title: Birth in Maida Vale, London
events.description: Alan Mathison Turing was born in Maida Vale, London, to Julius Mathison Turing and Ethel Sara Turing.

images.caption: Blue plaque marking Alan Turing's 1912 birthplace at the Colonnade Hotel, London.

location_coordinates.label: Maida Vale, London, Greater London, England, W9 1EU, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Maida Vale, London, England

events.date_note: The first day of term at Sherborne coincided with the 1926 General Strike; date approximated to the strike's start
events.title: Starts at Sherborne School
events.description: Turing entered Sherborne School, an independent boarding school in Dorset. Determined to attend despite the General Strike, he bicycled about 60 miles to school.

events.title: Death of Christopher Morcom
events.description: Turing's close friend and fellow pupil Christopher Morcom died from complications of bovine tuberculosis. The loss deeply affected Turing and intensified his focus on science and mathematics.

events.date_note: Elected a Fellow of King's College later in 1935 after his dissertation work was accepted in March
events.title: Elected Fellow of King's College, Cambridge
events.description: On the strength of his original dissertation on the Gaussian error function and related work, Turing was elected a Fellow of King's College, Cambridge.

images.caption: Statue of King Henry VI on the fountain in King's College Front Court, with King's College Chapel and Great St Mary's Church in the background.

location_coordinates.label: King's College (University of Cambridge), King's Parade, Newnham, Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, England, CB2 1ST, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: King's College, Cambridge, England

events.date_note: Completed and delivered the manuscript in May 1936; it was published later that year in two parts
events.title: Completes 'On Computable Numbers'
events.description: Turing finished and submitted his seminal paper 'On Computable Numbers, with an Application to the Entscheidungsproblem', introducing the abstract 'Turing machine' and establishing key limits of computation.

location_coordinates.label: Cambridge, Cambridgeshire, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Cambridge, England

events.date_note: Doctorate awarded in 1938; specific month/day not stated on the main source page
events.title: Doctorate from Princeton University
events.description: Turing earned his PhD at Princeton University under Alonzo Church with the thesis 'Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals'.

location_coordinates.label: Princeton, Mercer County, New Jersey, United States
location_coordinates.name: Princeton, New Jersey, United States

events.date_note: Reported to Bletchley Park the day after Britain declared war on Germany
events.title: Reports to Bletchley Park for codebreaking
events.description: Turing joined the Government Code and Cypher School at Bletchley Park, where he would play a central role in Allied cryptanalysis during World War II.

location_coordinates.label: Bletchley Park, Ultra Avenue, Old Bletchley, West Bletchley, Bletchley, Milton Keynes, City of Milton Keynes, England, MK3 6GY, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Bletchley Park, Buckinghamshire, England

events.date_note: Early British bombes became operational in March 1940
events.title: British bombe cryptanalytic machines become operational
events.description: Building on Polish pre-war methods, Turing designed key improvements leading to operational British bombes that helped find daily Enigma settings.

images.caption: Rebuilt example of a British bombe cryptanalytic machine used against Enigma ciphers.

location_coordinates.label: Bletchley Park, Ultra Avenue, Old Bletchley, West Bletchley, Bletchley, Milton Keynes, City of Milton Keynes, England, MK3 6GY, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Bletchley Park, Buckinghamshire, England

events.date_note: By 1941 Turing was leading Hut 8 on German naval Enigma
events.title: Leads Hut 8 on German naval Enigma
events.description: Turing headed Hut 8, developing methods such as Banburismus that significantly aided the decryption of German naval Enigma, crucial to the Battle of the Atlantic.

location_coordinates.label: Bletchley Park, Ultra Avenue, Old Bletchley, West Bletchley, Bletchley, Milton Keynes, City of Milton Keynes, England, MK3 6GY, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Bletchley Park, Buckinghamshire, England

events.date_note: After WWII, Turing joined NPL and began the ACE design work
events.title: Joins National Physical Laboratory; designs ACE
events.description: Turing joined the National Physical Laboratory and produced a pioneering design for a stored-program computer, the Automatic Computing Engine (ACE).

location_coordinates.label: National Physical Laboratory, Hampton Hill, London Borough of Richmond upon Thames, London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: National Physical Laboratory, Teddington, England

events.date_note: Announced in the 1946 New Year Honours
events.title: Appointed Officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE)
events.description: In recognition of his secret wartime service in cryptanalysis, Turing was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire.

images.caption: Alan Turing's Order of the British Empire (OBE) medal, held in the Sherborne School archives.

location_coordinates.label: London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: London, England

events.date_note: Appointed Reader in Mathematics and Deputy Director of the Computing Machine Laboratory
events.title: Joins the University of Manchester
events.description: Turing moved to the University of Manchester, contributing to the early Manchester computers and beginning research that connected computing with mathematical biology.

images.caption: University of Manchester blue plaque commemorating Alan Turing's role as Reader in Mathematics (1948–1954).

location_coordinates.label: University of Manchester, Oxford Road, Chorlton-on-Medlock, Manchester, Greater Manchester, England, M13 9PL, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: University of Manchester, Manchester, England

events.date_note: Published in the journal Mind in October 1950
events.title: Publishes 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'
events.description: Turing's influential paper introduced the imitation game (later known as the Turing test) as a criterion for machine intelligence.

location_coordinates.label: Manchester, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Manchester, England

events.date_note: Date of conviction for gross indecency
events.title: Convicted and accepts hormone treatment
events.description: Turing was prosecuted for homosexual acts and, following conviction, accepted hormone treatment (chemical castration) as an alternative to imprisonment.

location_coordinates.label: Manchester, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Manchester, England

events.date_note: Published in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society in 1952
events.title: Publishes 'The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis'
events.description: Turing's paper on reaction–diffusion systems founded a new approach in mathematical biology and predicted phenomena such as oscillating chemical reactions.

location_coordinates.label: Manchester, Greater Manchester, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Manchester, England

events.date_note: An inquest determined suicide; some analyses suggest accidental poisoning is also consistent with the evidence
events.title: Death from cyanide poisoning
events.description: Turing died at his home in Wilmslow from cyanide poisoning. He was 41.

location_coordinates.label: Wilmslow, Cheshire East, England, United Kingdom
location_coordinates.name: Wilmslow, Cheshire, England
